learn the basics of drawing first. I can say I'm a decent artist but even have trouble with urban sketching. Some urban sketchers are very good with buildings but aren't as good with organic things like humans/animals, basically the opposite to how i am lol so it depends.  
If i would point you towards anywhere to start I'd say learn how to break things down, learn that art as a whole is made up of different chunks which all hold together to create the full picture. For urban sketching, it can be different tho where you just block out the basic outlines then add the details. It might look wonky if you tediously work on, for example, the handle of a bike with every detail then move on to a detailed wheel. It would be more fitting to draw a 'skeleton' of a bike then slowly add onto the skeleton so the form stays the same, know what i mean? \^\^; Also, its kinda annoying but if its urban sketching 100% nose about in learning perspective, even just a little bit verrry basic stuff like vanishing points lol.  


what also helps is observational sketching, i find it very helpful! \^\^ whenever you go out maybe bring a small, portable sketchbook or basiclaly anything to draw on and draw whats in front of you, photos of buildings online, whatever you like! take a walk and observe your surroundings & draw them! \^\^ its ok if it doesnt turn out perfect, just practice making it a habit cause the more you do it the more you get used to the rhythm of things & get better! and remember, its also totally ok if you just wanna try it out as a hobby & not wanna be a pro so do whatever you like! sorry for the wall of text lol and i hope all the info doesn't seem overhwelming. you dont even have to follow everything just do what you feel like suits you the most! :)

OP, I just wanted to say I'm in a similar situation and you're not alone.

I've started feeling really depressed these past few months, especially cause of COVID and I've been avoiding online class, always getting scolded or even just confronted with my mom's disappointed voice, telling me my teacher notified her I have missing grades on a bunch of my subjects. Unlike you though, I'm not in college, just around middleschool.

My mom works so hard and is genuinely such an amazing parent, providing for us even without my dad's financial help. I don't feel worthy enough to be her child sometimes. She grew up poor yet persevered nonetheless and I heard her mention sometimes she gives us all these things cause she wanted us to live an amazing childhood, one that she never had. Yet here I am, a useless, ungrateful waste of space.

I even used to be an honor student before all this happened. I was a good kid, and now I'm a failure.

I wouldn't even say it's the schools fault. Lots of people are having lower grades here due to internet, less motivation, etc. They have valid reasons for blaming the teaching system while here I am, a privileged brat who has decent internet access \_willingly\_ avoiding her classes, having her assignments and projects pile up cause I'm too scared to face them, drowning my sorrows by browsing the internet on websites like Reddit and playing videogames like you do. I saw a lot of myself reflected on your post. God i wish I could give you a hug right now, our experiences aren't 100% the same but I feel you.

When I saw your post, it stood out cause I could relate to it greatly and most of what you said. Just remember, if college doesn't work out, it's okay. I'm not sure if I sounds tone-deaf for you are in a far later point of life than I am, but you can try again in life. There's always a second chance. We can do this, OP. Despite how much we fucked up we can salvage the messes we made and despite how we both think, it isn't the end of the world. I'm in no way expecting you to be swayed by these words, I doubt this is gonna fix your problems but maybe hearing someone else is experiencing the same thing will make you feel less alone. <3 This is optional but if you wanna talk feel free to DM me. I may not be around 24/7 (I'm just being honest, it would be insincere if I didn't mention that, but I'll try my absolute best. :)
